speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To begin, is this pain constant or does it come and go, and did it start after an injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; can you tell me if you have noticed any redness, warmth, or a visible lump on the swollen knee? Also, have you experienced any morning stiffness that lasts for more than 30 minutes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis (Left Knee)

The previous suggestion of a urinary tract infection is clinically inconsistent with localized knee swelling and severe nocturnal pain. We must rule out an infected joint immediately; please proceed with an urgent left knee aspiration and send the fluid for Gram stain and culture. REQUEST TEST: Left Knee Aspiration (Cell Count, Gram Stain, Culture, Crystal Analysis)
